title: Admin script-to-workflow adapter: safe, parameterized wrapper for ad-hoc ops scripts
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Support engineers and SREs routinely run ad-hoc admin scripts (shell/python) to remediate customer incidents or perform maintenance. These scripts live in repos and run locally or via internal CI, which makes auditing, dry-run validation, structured parameterization, and safe rollbacks difficult.

Goal: Build a lightweight adapter service and library that wraps arbitrary admin scripts in a consistent, typed workflow interface so they can be executed as discrete runbook tasks from the Console or operator CLI. The adapter must provide: parameter schemas, a dry-run mode with static checks, an execution sandbox with circuit-breakers/timeouts, audit provenance (who ran what, input values, outputs), automatic rollback hooks, and an approval gate for dangerous operations.

Why now: Increasing frequency of cross-team maintenance and several recent near-miss incidents (postmortem links in comments) indicate we need better guardrails and observability for ad-hoc admin actions. This feature reduces human error risk and enables reuse of existing scripts without requiring a full rewrite into a platform job.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Kickoff: design sync with PM (Amira Chen) and Security. Agreed scope: adapter + CLI shim; not building a full workflow engine — it will emit task metadata consumable by existing runbook runner.

2025-02-14 - Tech spike complete: created prototype wrapper that launches scripts in a restricted Docker sandbox with environment variable injection and a JSON parameter manifest. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admin-adapter/pull/5

2025-02-18 - Security review (initial): raised concerns about privileged mount access for certain scripts. Decided: adapter will require explicit allowlist per-script and runtime capability flags; non-allowlisted scripts run in strict-no-privilege mode.
2025-02-22 - PM review: Amira requested approval gating for 'delete'/'destroy' actions and a required 2-step confirmation for high-impact scripts. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-25 - Implementation kickoff: Ethan set up base service scaffold and the parameter-schema library. Data retention/audit log shape is being finalized with Observability team.
Follow-ups: add observability dashboard (latency, failures, approval wait times) and a migration plan for the 25 most used legacy scripts.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes a CLI and HTTP endpoint that accepts: script identifier, JSON inputs matching a registered schema, dry-run flag, and optional approval token.
Scripts must be registered with a manifest (owner, schema, allowlist flags, rollback hook). Registration stored in internal catalog (reads/writes via admin-api).
Dry-run executes static checks and a stubbed execution path without performing side-effects; returns validation report and simulated logs.
Execution occurs in a sandbox with enforced CPU/memory limits, timeouts, and capability restrictions; failures generate structured telemetry to Console.
Approval gate enforced for scripts with 'high-impact' label: request -> reviewer notification -> token issuance; token required to run real execution.
All runs emit auditable provenance records (user, timestamp, inputs, exit code, artifacts) retained per retention policy and viewable in Console run history.
Rollback hook executes automatically when script marks a failure and rollback exists; rollback runs under the same approval policy as original action.
Unit and integration tests cover: schema validation, dry-run behavior, allowlist enforcement, approval token flow, and basic rollback execution.
Migration doc for top-25 scripts and an onboarding guide for Support engineers completed.
implementation_notes: We will avoid building a full orchestration engine; instead adapter will produce a standard task envelope that the existing runbook/task-runner can consume. This reduces scope and leverages previous investments (see ENG-824999).
Sandbox approach: start with Docker-runner with seccomp profile + no-new-privileges. Plan subsequent migration to gVisor for stronger isolation if needed.
Parameter schemas will use JSON Schema draft-07 and we will provide a small TypeScript/Go codegen for CLI form rendering in Console.
Approval tokens are opaque JWTs signed by admin-api; tokens include script-id, permitted-user, and expiration. Tokens scoped per environment (prod vs staging).
Telemetry: emit structured events to the existing ops-telemetry stream with tags: script_id, outcome, duration, approver_id (if any). Integrate a Console view for recent runs and approval queues.

Trade-offs: initial implementation restricts to scripts that are containerizable; legacy scripts that require host mounts will be flagged and require manual migration or elevated review. This keeps initial safety guarantees strong.
risks_mitigation: Risk: scripts may still perform destructive operations in container if given wrong inputs. Mitigation: enforce parameter schema, approval gating, and default to dry-run for any schema change.
Risk: performance overhead from sandbox may increase run time. Mitigation: set pragmatic resource SLOs and surface latency in Console so teams can decide to run directly for low-risk quick ops.
Risk: owners may bypass system by running scripts directly. Mitigation: provide CLI convenience and audit incentives; gradually make Console the canonical way by improving UX and discovery.
Risk: secrets handling for scripts (DB creds, tokens). Mitigation: use secret placeholders with runtime injection from KMS-backed vault per-run and never allow raw secret strings in task inputs.
